sentences.text: The skull of this animal possesses several unique features not seen in other plesiosaurians. These include a dorsoventrally thick, mediolaterally expanded platform formed by the posteromedial processes of the premaxillae. The skull also has two closely spaced foramina on the lateral surface of the exoccipital. Additional unique traits involve a supplementary foramen penetrating the parietal sagittal crest, no contact between the pterygoid and vomer, and no contact between the pterygoids in the palate.
The genus name honors Mary Anning, a famous British fossil collector from Lyme Regis. The species name is derived from the Lyme Regis locality where the specimen was found.

The only known species, A. lymense, was discovered in Early Jurassic rocks at Lyme Regis in the United Kingdom. The animal is known only from holotype NHMUK OR 49202, a complete skull, palate, mandible, and eight associated cervical vertebrae. The fossil material represents a juvenile plesiosaur. The specimen was collected from Hettangian to early Sinemurian-aged beds of the Lower Lias Group at Lyme Regis, Dorset. Peggy Vincent and Roger B. J. Benson named the genus and its type species in 2012.

Anningasaura belongs to the order Plesiosauria. Phylogenetic analysis places Anningasaura as a basal, non-neoplesiosaurian plesiosaur. A phylogenetic analysis by Benson et al. (2012) determined it was a basal non-neoplesiosaurian plesiosaur.
Anningasaura lived from the Hettangian to the Pliensbachian, between 201.4 and 184.2 million years ago.
